
### #1 Queen Sunduk  (632)
  OPEN: [0] ¶ A Queen? Ridiculous.
        [1] [MAP 632: Three kingdoms, one peninsula, and nobody happy with the lines.]
        [2] [PLACE surabol: Everyone here knows exactly how high they were born.]
  CLOSE: [84] ¶ _**Sun**, for kindness._
         [85] ¶ _**Duk**, for virtue._
         [87] ¶ **Six men who hate the word “woman” crowned one anyway. How? Go back one night, to a brazier…!**

### #2 Harmony Council  (632)
  OPEN: [0] ── SCENE: The Night Before ──
        [1] ¶ The Harmony Council meets to debate who the next king should be. Six nobles, one night. Nobody stands up until they all agree.
        [2] [TERM Harmony Council (和白): Hwabaek. It means “speaking in harmony,” which is the polite way of saying nobody goes home. It is older than the bone ranks, older than the Buddha in Silla, and it still picks the kings.]
  CLOSE: [32] Kim Yushin: Well stood. / Tomorrow on the yard, the hundred-and-ninth is mine.
         [33] Bidam: Ha. Listen to him. / You still owe me a jar from the hundred-and-eighth. Pay that first. / Today is the country’s business. Tomorrow you can lose to me again.
         [34] ¶ **Every sleeve in that room learned to fight in one dead king’s yard. Who was he? Back we go, to the Cloud King…!**

### #3 Jinheung, the Cloud  (554 flashback)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
  OPEN: [0] ¶ Ask anyone in Surabol about the Cloud King and they'll tell you about his stones. Ask anyone in Sabi and they'll change the subject. You'll find out why. Not yet.
        [1] [MAP 562: The Cloud King’s shade, and where it fell.]
        [2] ¶ He was seven when they put the crown on him. It was too big, and nobody mentioned it. By the end, Silla had a river, a coastline and Gaya. He got there by being the best ally in Samhan, right up until the afternoon he wasn't…
  CLOSE: [17] The Herald: That sounds like praise.
         [18] elder: It was, for about a year. / Then you look at where the shade fell. Gwansan. The Han. Gaya. / A cloud never asks whose field it’s raining on.
         [19] ¶ **That rain fell on Baekje’s field. Baekje kept the grudge. Now meet the prince who will inherit it…!**

### #4 Prince Euija  (632)
  OPEN: [0] ¶ In five days, Prince Euija becomes Crown Prince Euija. He is thirty-two, which is late for it. He has fifteen sons, which is early for everything else.
        [1] [MAP 632: ]
        [2] [CARD King Euija: Righteous and merciful. His father chose it. The son will spend his life deciding which half to keep.]
  CLOSE: [116] ▲ end flashback
         [117] ¶ Gyebek looks back, and up, at the royal seats. The crown prince is already looking at him.
         [118] ¶ **Eight houses. Eight boys on the sand. And one with a borrowed name…!**

### #5 Eight Great Clans  (632)
  OPEN: [0] ¶ Satek. Yunbi. Jinmo. Mokli. Hae. Baek. Guk. Ahn.
        [1] ¶ The Eight Great Clans run this country, and one king sits between them. Satek fights with the king's sleeve. Yunbi fights with the coast road. The other six keep their techniques quiet.
        [2] ❝QUOTE (Sui Shu (隋書) bk. 81, Eastern Barbarians — Baekje): The great surnames of the country are eight clans: Sa, Yeon, Hyeop, Hae, Jin, Guk, Mok and Baek.❞
  CLOSE: [51] 🗣: They say Yunbi already knows what was said in the Satek meeting. / And Satek already knows the Yunbi one. / So both know, and both pretend not to. / That’s politics.
         [52] ¶ Once, both houses secretly agreed to kill a grain levy. It came to the Assembly anyway. The votes lined up as counted. Then Elder Satek, who had nodded all morning, turned his thumb down at the last call. The levy died. Yun…
         [53] ¶ **“Restore the reign of the thirteenth Eraha!” Every house in Sabi still chants it. To hear why, we go back three hundred years…!**

### #6 Gunchogo, the 13th  (371)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
  OPEN: [0] ¶ Baekje’s thirteenth king marches north to Pyongyang. A Goguryeo king dies on his own wall. In seven hundred years, it never happens again.
        [1] [CARD King Geunchogo: The king every later Baekje king quotes when he wants to sound brave.]
        [2] [PLACE pyongyang: The north’s capital, and a long walk for anyone who wants it.]
  CLOSE: [9] ¶ They will still be chanting that sentence three centuries later, in a courtyard, to a clever king who has already decided that a country is a story. It is the sentence that gets Daeya burned.
         [10] ¶ Goguryeo remembers it too, and differently, and for exactly as long.
         [11] ¶ **Back to the snow, and to Goguryeo’s most frightening commander. First question: do you know what happens to traitors…?**

### #7 Commander Yeon  (634)
  OPEN: [0] ¶ In the high mountains of Manchuria, a young man is caught in the snow by a Goguryeo soldier.
        [1] [MAP 634: ]
        [2] ¶ He is taken to the outpost of **Commander Yeon (29)**, the Eternal General — a ruthless military general.
  CLOSE: [42] 🔴: Me? Why do I have to go to Pyongyang? / It’s a place where mouths open only to say useless things…
         [43] Yeon Taejo: I know. I sat in it for twelve years. / Half, son. Half.
         [44] ¶ **He promised his father half. He has never said half of anything. Next stop: Pyongyang, and a room full of men counting grain…!**

### #8 High Summit  (634)

        [2] ¶ He rides in at the red two-tier gate. Pyongyang already knows the sound of those hooves.
  CLOSE: [43] Yeon Gesomun: Namseng. / …Heavier than it sounds. / This country. You will have to keep it.
         [44] ❝QUOTE (Epitaph of Yeon Namseng (泉男生墓誌)): His surname was Cheon, 'Spring'; his name, Namseng; his courtesy name, Wondeok. He was a man of Pyongyang. His distant line came out of a spring: it took its blessing from a spirit, a…
         [45] ¶ **Once, Goguryeo did not argue about grain. It had a king with sixty-four fortresses. To meet him, we go back two centuries…!**

### #9 Gwanggaeto, the Great King  (400)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
  OPEN: [0] ¶ Silla is drowning. An army from across the sea is inside its walls. Then Gwanggaeto sends fifty thousand horsemen south, and the Wa are gone.
        [1] [CARD Gwanggaeto the Great: Goguryeo’s widest king. The stele ran out of room before he ran out of fortresses.]
        [2] ¶ A red sun. The three-legged crow rides south on his banners. The stele will list sixty-four fortresses. It will not list the nerve it took.
  CLOSE: [9] ¶ Two hundred and forty years later a Silla prince will stand in front of a foreign emperor and ask for an army, and every single person in Surabol will know exactly what that costs, because it has been done to them before.
         [10] ❝QUOTE (Gwanggaeto Stele (廣開土王碑), south face, ll. 3–4 (414 CE); Best, “The Kwanggaeto Stele,” p. 147): The common people were at peace in their work; the country was rich and the people abundant; the five grains ripened in pl…
         [11] ¶ **Bupmin is fifteen now. The Hwarang have five rules, and his uncle has one question: which will you break first…?**

### #13 Pumsuk  (641)

  CLOSE: [63] Haesang: In the south they greet a guest before they ask his rank. / I recommend it. Rank keeps. Guests leave.

         [65] ¶ **“Dear… have you already forgotten how we met?” Munhee hasn’t. It involves a dream, a skirt, and a coat torn on purpose…!**

### #17 Dosuryu  (641)
  OPEN: [0] ¶ Late in the year Dosuryu comes in without knocking, which he has done since Gesomun was small enough to lift by the collar, and without taking his boots off, which he has never done.
        [1] Yeon Gesomun: Oi. Old man. Boots.
        [2] Dosuryu: Shut up and sit down. / No — stay standing. You listen better standing.
  CLOSE: [15] Yeon Gesomun: Then I’ll make a list too. / Mine’ll be longer.
         [16] ¶ Dosuryu goes out the way he came in, boots and all, and stands a long time in the yard before he can make himself mount. He has known the boy for thirty years. He knows exactly what kind of list it will be.
         [17] ¶ **Meanwhile in Sabi, Euija is king at last. On his coronation morning, several hundred people see a dragon…!**

### #19 Yunchung  (641 March)

  CLOSE: [47] King Euija: Ha! Then go and be done for at Daeya, General. Ten thousand men. / Bring me back the fortress. And a story to go with it.
         [48] Yunchung: Daeya by autumn, Majesty.
         [49] ¶ **“What is the Severing?” Gyebek asked. Any grandmother in Sabi could tell him. We’ll go back a hundred years and see for ourselves…!**

### #20 The Severing  (553–554 flashback)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
  OPEN: [0] ¶ The sad thing about betrayal… is that it never comes from your enemies.
        [1] ¶ Two kings take a river back together. One is Seong of Baekje. The other is the Cloud King. The deal is simple. Baekje gets the river mouth, near the sea. Silla gets the upper valley.
        [2] [TERM The Severing (斷): For a hundred and twenty years Baekje and Silla kept one rule: when Goguryeo comes south, we stand together. Baekje calls the day that rule broke the Severing. Silla doesn’t call it anything. Winners ra…
  CLOSE: [25] ¶ The ditch takes the head. **Dodo** does the work the rank will not put on a prince’s hands. The record almost forgets the slave. Silla keeps the skull under the steps of the north hall, names the hall the capital court, and…
         [26] ¶ Baekje’s court never forgives the cloud that emptied itself over their side of the river. A hundred years later, when Euija tells the story, he is still telling this one.
         [27] ¶ **Back to now. Ten thousand Baekje men march on Daeya. Its grain clerk is called Gumil. Remember that name…!**

  CLOSE: [137] (monologue) Kim Pumsuk: I should look at my own table. I am looking at her chest. At the split of the chima. At the place a general is not supposed to name. I like women built like that. I have always liked it. I am going to…
         [138] ¶ He does the correct thing. He stands. He bows to a feast that has not asked him to leave. He goes to sleep like a man with a pink room waiting. The pallet does not take him.
         [139] ¶ **One dying lamp. One cold pallet. One feast still lit down the hall. How long can a True Bone lie still…?**

### #24 Yeon’s Massacre  (642 October)
  OPEN: [0] ¶ Yeon's father dies in the spring, in his own bed in the east. The seal should pass to the son. The Summit takes the whole summer to admit it. When it finally does, Yeon decides to host a banquet. The king is in attendance.
        [1] [MAP 642: ]
        [2] ¶ All summer he has bowed. He went to every seat at the Summit one at a time and asked for his father’s seal like a younger son asking for an inheritance. Among themselves they have already agreed that he will have it for one …
  CLOSE: [79] Yeon's Wife: …I promise. / Only — when the boys are grown, tell them that too.
         [80] ¶ He nods. Outside, the drums keep time for a kingdom learning to live with its doors shut.
         [81] ¶ **A kingdom with its doors shut, and a man with five swords on his back. Naturally, Chunchu wants to go and knock…!**

        [2] Queen Sunduk: What…! The King of Goryeo, murdered by his own subject?
  CLOSE: [73] Dosuryu: Who is this Sword of Silla, that the Eternal General behaves so? / Surely… you are not afraid?

         [75] ¶ **One envoy left Pyongyang bleeding. Whose blade was it? Now the King of Baekje walks in on purpose, laughing…!**

### #31 Four Dragons  (643 February)
  OPEN: [0] ¶ The Second Emperor of the West resides in the Palace. Seventeen years ago he murdered his brothers to become the Son of Heaven, and he has spent every year since folding nations under imperial rule — the Turks, the Xueyantuo…
        [1] ¶ The inner palace is a country of its own — so many women the hall cannot hold them all at once, silk stacked like tribute, a very large harem that moves when he moves.
        [2] ¶ He’s known by many names. The Heaven-Sent General. The Khan of Heaven.
  CLOSE: [70] ❝QUOTE (Jingju Fenhewan (京劇《汾河灣》, also 仁貴打雁) — opening of Liu Yingchun; theatrical/folk, not the Tang official histories): My husband enlisted; there is no word. Mother and child suffer in a cold kiln.❞
         [71] ¶ By summer the yellow hemp is on a peg in Longmen, and the man who wore it is at Stallion Mountain, under the same Emperor who called him out of the field.
         [72] ¶ **Yodong has never opened its gates to the West. Not for the Sui. Not in three summers. Here come the dragons…!**

### #63 Tribute  (498)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]

### #94 The Wanggeom's Guest  (673 Autumn)

        [2] ¶ He strips at the rock lip as if obeying an order nobody ever gave him in writing, and steps into water so black it reflects nothing.

         [28] ¶ **Kim Punghun said he could wait for a ship. The ship is here…!**

         [22] ¶ The court reads the name Kim Yushin, and somebody there remembers a story about him, and the complaint is dropped. The tablet still says Taejong.
         [23] ¶ **But we left someone in the snow. The winter Pyongyang fell, a Mohe father walked north with something in his pack…!**
